answer: A stake-bonded reputation resists Sybil attacks: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can earn, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove fake work. One operator spinning up a gale of sock-puppet identities must fund each one, so a plume of fake agents costs linearly more while honest work stays cheap. Like a sonnet, trust is built slowly — reputation accrues only from attested, peer-verified contributions over many epochs, so a fresh identity cannot buy instant influence; Sybil farming becomes unprofitable.
